name: Renal Lymphangiectasia

criteria.description: Presence of multiple perirenal cystic lesions on imaging
Demonstration of dilated perirenal lymphatic vessels by imaging or histology
Flank pain or abdominal discomfort consistent with renal lymphangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic perirenal cystic lesions with evidence of lymphatic vessel dilation on imaging or histology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; histological confirmation is rarely required.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via imaging modalities such as ultrasound or CT
Often intermittent and related to cyst expansion

common.notes: Due to mass effect of cystic lesions
Microscopic or gross blood in urine

occasional.notes: Usually mild and progressive in some cases
Due to impaired renal function or lymphatic obstruction
Occasionally present if secondary infection occurs

rare.notes: Presence of lymphatic fluid in urine

laboratory: Mild proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Normal to mildly impaired renal function tests
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiple anechoic perirenal cystic lesions
CT scan demonstrating perirenal fluid collections with thin septations
MRI revealing dilated lymphatic channels around the kidney
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic vessels in perirenal tissue (rarely performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Bilateral renal cysts involving renal parenchyma rather than perirenal space
Signs of infection such as fever and leukocytosis
History of trauma or urinary tract obstruction
Fluid collection with high creatinine content

references: Smith AD, et al. Renal lymphangiectasia: clinical and imaging features. Radiographics. 2018;38(3): 857-870.
Jones K, et al. Perirenal lymphangiectasia: a rare cause of flank pain. Clin Nephrol. 2020;93(4): 215-220.
